answers.explanation: Time division multiple access: each station gets a time slot in each round.
A fixed-length slot equal to one packet's transmission time, once per round.
Unused slots go idle: that's channel partitioning's big inefficiency.
Each slot belongs to one station. That's what keeps TDMA collision-free, and what wastes capacity.
The spectrum is split into frequency bands, one per station.
Each station has its own band, and they all transmit at the same time.
All stations share the same time and frequencies. The codes separate them.
That's the trick: the receiver separates them by code, not by time or frequency.
The same problem as circuit switching in Chapter 1: reserved capacity wasted on silence.
